java.question: In Java, what is the best description of a **class** vs an **object**?
options: A class is a running program; an object is a file on disk
A class is a blueprint/type; an object is a concrete instance of that type
A class and an object are the same thing
An object defines methods; a class only stores numbers
java.explanation: A class describes the structure and behavior; each object is one instance created from that class.

python.question: In Python, what is the best description of a **class** vs an **object** (instance)?

A class is a blueprint/type; an object is a concrete instance of that type
A class and an object are the same thing
An object defines methods; a class only stores numbers
python.explanation: A class describes the structure and behavior; each object is one instance created from that class.

java.question: What does **encapsulation** usually mean in OOP?

Making every field public so other classes can edit it freely
Inheriting from multiple parents at once
java.explanation: Encapsulation hides internal state and lets the object enforce rules through its methods.

java.question: Which approach best checks whether a list contains **any duplicate** values in roughly O(n) time (on average)?
options: Compare every pair with nested loops only
Add each value to a HashSet and see if an insert was already present
Sort is impossible for this problem
java.explanation: A set remembers what you have already seen, so you can detect a repeat in one pass (average O(n)).

python.question: Which approach best checks whether a list contains **any duplicate** values in roughly O(n) time (on average)?
options: Compare every pair with nested loops only
Add each value to a set and see if it was already present
Sorting is impossible for this problem
python.explanation: A set remembers what you have already seen, so you can detect a repeat in one pass (average O(n)).

java.question: To check whether an array contains a duplicate, you can either (A) compare every pair of indexes with nested loops, or (B) scan once while storing seen values in a HashSet. What does approach (A) mainly cost more of?
options: Memory only — nested loops use more RAM
Time — comparing many pairs is often O(n²)
Nothing — they always have identical performance
java.explanation: Pairwise comparison grows with n²; a set-based scan is typically much faster for large n, at the cost of some extra memory.

python.question: To check whether a list contains a duplicate, you can either (A) compare every pair of indexes with nested loops, or (B) scan once while storing seen values in a set. What does approach (A) mainly cost more of?
options: Memory only — nested loops use more RAM
Time — comparing many pairs is often O(n²)
Nothing — they always have identical performance
python.explanation: Pairwise comparison grows with n²; a set-based scan is typically much faster for large n, at the cost of some extra memory.

python.question:
This code counts **clumps**: contiguous runs of length ≥ 2 of equal values. What is `clumps` for the list shown?

```python
a = [1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3]
clumps = 0
i = 0
while i < len(a):
    j = i
    while j < len(a) and a[j] == a[i]:
        j += 1
    if j - i >= 2:
        clumps += 1
    i = j
```
python.explanation: Three clumps: three 1s, two 2s, and three 3s.
